intended_object: For open normal subgroups N ≤ M of a topological group G and a topological G-representation X, this is the inclusion X^M ↪ X^N of invariants, seen as a continuous morphism of G/N-representations, with X^M made a G/N-representation by inflation along G/N → G/M. It is the transition map in the direct system (G/U, X^U) whose colimit computes continuous cohomology. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The underlying map takes the subtype inclusion of the M-invariants, which is a continuous linear map, and restricts its codomain to the N-invariants. This is legitimate because N ≤ M: a vector fixed by M is fixed by N (`x.2 ⟨t.1, hNM t.2⟩`). The source is `res (quotientTransitionHom N M hNM) (quotientInvariants M X)`, i.e. X^M with G/N acting through G/N → G/M. The target is X^N with its residual G/N action. Equivariance holds by definition: on a coset gN both sides act by X.ρ g, and the proof checks this on representatives. This is the standard inflation-type coefficient map X^M → X^N between quotient stages.

On generality: the construction would also make sense for arbitrary normal subgroups, since the projection G/N → G/M is continuous for the quotient topologies. But the indexing by open normal subgroups is the standard setting for the colimit description of continuous or profinite cohomology, and the companion map `quotientTransitionHom` uses discreteness of G/N. So the restriction is natural, not an unjustified narrowing. Mathlib has no counterpart for topological representations.
